result.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Bias in MLLM for Long Video Understanding
result.summary: Long-video question answering is challenging since the answer often hinges on a few decisive moments scattered throughout the video, while memory constraints force Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to sample frames at extremely low rates, resulting in sparsity that risks omitting key evidence. Though aggressively enlarging the context size is intuitive, we argue that performance remains fundamentally constrained by the bias, \emph{i.e.}, the misleading cues caused by spurious \textit{linguistic} correlations and salient yet irrelevant \textit{visual} observations. In this paper, we first introduce {S-MME}, a benchmark designed to systematically diagnose shortcut-biased behavior in MLLMs. To mitigate this failure, we further propose a training-free framework, Counterfactual Long-video Evidence-Aware Reasoning (CLEAR). By treating the full video-question pair as a complete view, CLEAR estimates bias effects via augmented views by only keeping the question or locally salient visual clips. Then, we intervene hidden states to mitigate the discrepancy at inference such that the correct answer can be predicted confidently. With experimental studies across five benchmarks, we show that our method is generalizable and can be integrated in different MLLMs, yielding consistent gains in prediction and robustness. We hope CLEAR can offer a complementary direction in test-time scaling for long-video understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对长视频问答中低帧率采样带来的稀疏性，提出基准 S-MME 诊断 MLLM 因语言虚假关联与显著无关视觉片段产生的捷径偏差，并提出免训练框架 CLEAR：以「问题」或「局部显著片段」构造增强视图估计偏置效应，再在推理期干预 hidden states 以抑制偏差、提升答案置信度。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉证据筛选与「模型是否真正使用视觉内容」，其推理期 hidden state 干预与 test-time scaling 视角可供核查：偏置校正是否等价于更有效地利用关键证据、以及是否会误删有用视觉信息。
